summary: A sound, rules-clean stage-1 rewrite of the sliding-layer attention back end. The turn_1 and turn_4 targets are physically reachable, and the T=16384 timing gate protects first_turn. No landed hypothesis confounds it, so no companions are needed. The main gap: the incumbent's q-cast and FusedRMSNormGate rows are hidden in the profile's '... 11 more', so prepare() should time the incumbent sequence beside the new one at the scored turn shapes.
justification: Mechanism is plausible. Master profile ba9c16b9cc6b4605 confirms FA3 at 25.3 us plus FlashAttnFwdCombine at 7.1 us on sliding turn_1, 63.1 us at sliding turn_4 and 300.6 us at sliding first_turn. At turn_1, 96 per-head 128-row tiles do not fill 132 SMs and the work is latency-chain bound. GQA packing gives 16 tokens x 8 heads = 128 MMA rows per program and halves K/V gathers; with the 4-way split at turn_1 that makes 384 programs of about 8 64-key tiles each, against about 17 serial 128-key tiles in FA3. The ~15 us turn_1 target is credible. The window K/V working set (about 0.7 MB cold) is L2-resident and per-program gathers are latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound, so the LESSONS 2.1 TB/s gather ceiling does not bind. Floors check out: 4*753*2048*16*64 = 6.3 GFLOP, which is 6.4 us at 989 TF, with exp count at the same order. The expected directions match TASK weights. turn_1 is sliding 46 + full 16, about 72.4 ms per load, so saving ~22 us x 46 is about 1.4% on that load; turn_4 is about 0.6% of its load; first_turn is flat or gated. The headline gain is therefore about 0.6-0.7%, inside the +/-1.5% CI, as the hypothesis itself says. That is acceptable because, as a rewrite, it is judged on the replaced kernel rows. Weakest link: the incumbent's 'q cast + FusedRMSNormGate 2-5 us each' is an estimate, not in the profile. Both rows fall into '... 11 more' at turn_1 and turn_4, as the new combine kernel likely will too, so milestone 2 (at or below the incumbent kernels' time) cannot be fully read from top_kernels without extra prints. Secondary weak links: (a) the 'combine folded in' saving at turn_1 is partly given back by the stage's own split-combine launch; (b) a Triton bf16-dot FA at first_turn will very likely lose to FA3, so the gate will keep FA3 there; that is expected and fine.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: not a confounder but the incumbent definition. It established the exact q.to(FP8) + paged FA3 (window (2047,0)) + FusedRMSNormGate sequence being replaced and used as the self-check oracle; nothing tunable in it alters this comparison.

experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 and experts-hybrid-marlin-turn-triton-first-turn: touch only prepare()/_experts after the o GEMM. The timed replay starts with a cold L2 and the attention block runs strictly before the experts on the main stream, so they share no memory traffic, numerical path or launch adjacency with the replaced kernels. A change in attention kernel time is not caused by them. The only weak coupling is that master's prepare() spends time on expert self-checks, which shares the 300 s prepare and 15 min run budget with this hypothesis's T=16384 graph timing and self-checks.
interference: No companion is warranted. No landed hypothesis touches the sliding-attention back end, its inputs (qkv GEMM, FusedQKNorm, store_cache stay byte-identical) or its consumer (o GEMM unchanged). A gain or loss on the replaced rows is therefore attributable to the change itself. Full-layer shapes are a built-in control because they stay byte-identical. The first_turn sub-change is self-isolating through the prepare() timing gate and the PATH CHOSEN line. An ab-revert of a landed experts hypothesis would not change the attention rows, and a control splitting 'GQA kernel' from 'fused norm-gate epilogue' would cost a check to attribute about 2-5 us, which the next stage can do more cheaply. For a rewrite, the next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: No hard violation found. Queries rounded to E4M3 and no coarser, K/V read as FP8, P in BF16 (finer than FA3's FP8 P), no weight touched, every in-window key attended (only tiles wholly outside every row's window are skipped, which is standard sliding-window semantics, not block-skipping by score).

Split-KV at turn_1: a split whose key range is empty for some rows (early tokens at ctx=0, or splits that fall wholly outside a row's window) must write m=-inf and l=0, and the combine must treat them as zero weight without producing NaN. A NaN here fails the run, and because the self-check uses synthetic cases that may not include every split/empty pattern, add a ctx=0 split case (B=1 ctx=0 small L with S=4 forced).

Every launch must stay graph-capturable. Per-request key ranges come from device tensors (cache_seqlens/cu_seqlens_q/positions), and the split count S comes only from the config. The workspace sized for T<=4096 must cover every config that selects S>1, which holds because S>1 only when B*ceil(L/16)*2 < 264. Assert that in prepare().

The first_turn decision is made in prepare() on synthetic data (shape-based routing, not derived from data), which is allowed. Keep the decision a Python dict keyed by T so kernel_fn branches only on config.

If the FP8xFP8 tl.dot for S is used, k_scale must be applied in the fp32 softmax scale (as planned), never by rescaling the cache. If FP8 P were ever tried, it would match FA3's FP8 P, which is still allowed, but the plan keeps BF16.
open_questions: The incumbent q.to(FP8) and FusedRMSNormGate rows, and the new combine kernel, will likely be hidden in the profile's '... 11 more' at turn_1 and turn_4. Should prepare() also time master's exact sequence and the new path as captured graphs at the scored turn_1 (B=1 ctx=80000 L=753) and turn_4 (B=4) shapes (cold L2, median), printing both, so milestone 2 is readable from the log?

Is the 2e-2 rel-L2-vs-incumbent pass bar safe, given that the incumbent uses FP8 P and the new kernel uses BF16 P? The difference after per-head RMSNorm and gating should be well under 1e-2, but if the bar trips spuriously the run silently becomes byte-identical to master and wastes a rewrite check. Print the margin.

At turn_1 the 4-way split adds a combine launch. Was S=2 or S=1 with BLOCK_TOK=16 (96 programs) considered as an alternative recorded in prepare() timing? A small in-prepare sweep over S in {1,2,4} at the turn_1 shape would choose from data at no check cost.

Does the profile show master's FA3 launching with PDL? Replacing it with non-PDL Triton launches could lose a few us of overlap with the neighbouring qk_norm/store_cache and o GEMM, which would show up as noise in the per-kernel rows.

Budget: the T=16384 synthetic self-check plus graph timing with a 256 MiB flush x 20 replays for both paths, on top of master's existing expert checks. Confirm prepare() stays well under 300 s and the whole run under 15 min including the Triton compile.
